form_de0a4def7aa4fdc5.title: National Scholarship Portal (NSP) — Post-Matric & Merit Scholarship Guidelines

chunks.title: Annual Family Income Criteria & Income Certificate
chunks.contentText: Total annual family income from all sources must not exceed Rs 2,50,000 per annum for scholarship eligibility. Self-employed guardians or agricultural workers must submit an income certificate issued by a competent revenue authority (Tahsildar, Revenue Inspector or Executive Magistrate). Salary slips or Form 16 are required for salaried parents.

chunks.title: Aadhaar Card Seeding & Bank Account Requirements
chunks.contentText: Scholarship disbursements are credited strictly via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). The applicant or guardian bank account must be an active savings account in a scheduled commercial bank seeded with the applicant Aadhaar number. Joint accounts with third parties or dormant accounts are rejected.

chunks.title: Social Category and Domicile Certificate
chunks.contentText: Applicants applying under SC, ST, OBC, or Minority categories must provide a valid digital caste certificate verifying their quota status. A valid State Domicile Certificate is mandatory to prove state residency for state-quota scholarship schemes.

chunks.title: Academic Records, Previous Marks & Roll Number
chunks.contentText: Applicants must have secured a minimum of 50% marks in the previous qualifying annual examination. The previous board roll number and institution code must match official education board registries.

form_ec891d8424c6b3da.title: Reserve Bank of India — Master Direction on Know Your Customer (KYC)

chunks.title: Permanent Account Number (PAN) & Form 60 Guidelines
chunks.contentText: Under Rule 114B of Income Tax Rules 1962, quoting PAN is mandatory for opening bank accounts and conducting financial transactions exceeding specified limits. Individuals who do not possess a PAN must submit Form 60 along with valid declaration of agricultural or exempt income.

chunks.title: Aadhaar Card as Officially Valid Document (OVD)
chunks.contentText: Aadhaar is accepted as an Officially Valid Document (OVD) for proof of identity and proof of address. Customers submitting physical copies of Aadhaar are permitted to mask the first eight digits of their Aadhaar number to protect personal privacy, leaving only the last four digits visible.

chunks.title: Mother Maiden Name and Security Verification
chunks.contentText: Banks collect confidential non-public biographical data, such as Mother Maiden Name, solely as a secondary authentication factor and security question for resetting credentials, tele-banking verification, and fraud prevention. It is never shared with third parties.

chunks.title: Current and Permanent Address Proof Requirements
chunks.contentText: Where the permanent address differs from the current residential address, an Officially Valid Document or utility bill (electricity, water, telephone piped gas) not older than two months may be accepted as proof of current address.

form_5fbbba0db7799ad1.title: CERT-In & RBI Advisory on Digital Payment Security & Phishing

chunks.title: One-Time Password (OTP) & PIN Confidentiality Notice
chunks.contentText: Never enter your One-Time Password (OTP), ATM PIN, UPI MPIN, or Card CVV on any website that is unencrypted (HTTP) or hosted on a third-party non-banking domain. Banks and government agencies will never ask for your card PIN or OTP during simple identity registrations.

chunks.title: Cross-Domain Form Submissions & Phishing Indicators
chunks.contentText: Be cautious of web forms that submit user data to a different external domain than the one shown in your browser address bar. Phishing sites frequently mimic legitimate government or banking portals while exfiltrating credentials to attacker-controlled server endpoints.
